bun-ca-cay-hai-phong.name: Spicy fish noodle soup, Hải Phòng style
bun-ca-cay-hai-phong.serving_basis: Four bowls of noodles with fried tilapia, fish cake, elephant ear stem and tangy, mildly spicy tomato broth.
bun-ca-cay-hai-phong.description: Hải Phòng spicy fish noodles pair a clear bone broth, colored with tomato and chili, with turmeric-seasoned fried tilapia, fish cake, elephant ear stem and rice vermicelli. Bếp Việt has adapted a home-cooking version with adjustable heat.
bun-ca-cay-hai-phong.finished_dish: The clear broth is savory from the bones, gently sour from tamarind and fragrant with mild chili. Golden fried fish keeps its flaky texture alongside soft noodles and crisp elephant ear stem.
bun-ca-cay-hai-phong.serving: Blanch the noodles, arrange the fried fish, fish cake and elephant ear stem in bowls, then ladle over hot broth. Serve with fresh herbs, banana blossom and chili sauce so everyone can adjust the heat.
bun-ca-cay-hai-phong.image_alt: A bowl of Hải Phòng spicy fish noodles with golden fried tilapia, fish cake, elephant ear stem and tomato broth.
bun-ca-cay-hai-phong.time_note: Simmering time depends on the type of bone; Fish needs to be fully cooked.
tips: Pat the fish completely dry before coating it so the crust turns crisp and the oil does not splatter.
Blanch the elephant ear stem with a little salt, rinse and gently squeeze to reduce irritation.
Add tamarind and chili gradually; the sour, spicy notes should lift the bone broth without overpowering the fish.
keywords: Spicy fish noodle soup, Hải Phòng style

ingredients.name: Tilapia fillet
ingredients.notes: Remove the bones and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Fish bones
ingredients.notes: Use the bones left after filleting the fish.

ingredients.name: Banana blossom
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly and soak in diluted lime water.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: For preparing and marinating the fish.

ingredients.name: Ripe tamarind
ingredients.notes: Soak in hot water and strain the juice.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying; pan-frying is also an option.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For simmering and adjusting the broth.

preparation_steps: Blanch the pork bones, rinse them, then add to a pot with water and ginger; rinse the fish bones.
Cut the fish into bite-size pieces and marinate with ginger and a little salt for 15 minutes. Prepare the tomatoes, elephant ear stem and accompaniments.
Soak the banana blossom in diluted lime water. Chop the dill and scallions, and slice the fish cake.
cooking_steps: Simmer the pork and fish bones over low heat for about 40 minutes, skimming for a clear broth. Remove the bones and strain if needed.
Sauté the shallots, then cook the tomatoes until soft and add them to the pot. Add tamarind liquid, fish sauce, salt, sugar and chili paste; taste and adjust.
Lightly coat the fish in flour and fry until golden and fully cooked. Blanch the elephant ear stem and fish cake in the hot broth until just tender.
Blanch the noodles and divide among bowls. Arrange the fish, fish cake and elephant ear stem on top, ladle over the broth, garnish with scallions and dill, and serve hot.

keywords: Spicy fish noodle soup, Hải Phòng style

nem-cua-be-hai-phong.name: Hải Phòng square crab spring rolls
nem-cua-be-hai-phong.serving_basis: Eight square rolls served with fresh rice vermicelli, herbs and sweet-and-sour fish sauce.
nem-cua-be-hai-phong.description: Nem cua bể is Hải Phòng’s palm-sized square spring roll. Its filling combines sea crab, pork, glass noodles, wood ear and shiitake mushrooms, egg and vegetables. Bếp Việt has adapted the square-folding and frying method for home kitchens.
nem-cua-be-hai-phong.finished_dish: Crisp golden rice-paper wrappers enclose sweet crab, tender glass noodles and a well-seasoned filling; garlic-lime dipping sauce balances the richness.
nem-cua-be-hai-phong.serving: Serve whole or halved while hot, with rice vermicelli, lettuce, herbs and sweet-and-sour fish sauce.
nem-cua-be-hai-phong.image_alt: Golden, crisp square Hải Phòng crab rolls, one cut open to show the crab filling, served with herbs and dipping sauce.
nem-cua-be-hai-phong.time_note: Frying time depends on spring roll thickness and oil temperature; The filling needs to be evenly heated before serving.
tips: Drain the noodles, mushrooms and vegetables well before mixing so the wrappers stay crisp.
Do not overfill or wrap too tightly; seal the square edges so the filling stays inside while frying.
Fry over medium heat and turn evenly so the filling heats through before the wrapper gets too dark.
keywords: Hải Phòng square crab spring rolls

ingredients.name: Ground pork

ingredients.name: Dried glass noodles
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft and cut into short lengths.

ingredients.name: Dried wood ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until expanded, then slice into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Dried shiitake mushrooms

ingredients.name: Fish sauce

ingredients.name: Sugar

ingredients.name: Cooking oil

preparation_steps: Soak the glass noodles and mushrooms until soft; drain and chop. Prepare the carrot, onion, bean sprouts and scallions.
Mix the pork with egg, glass noodles, wood ear and shiitake mushrooms, bean sprouts, carrot, onion, fish sauce, salt and pepper.
Pick the crab into bite-size pieces and set aside to divide evenly among the rolls. Prepare the square wrappers and serving herbs.
cooking_steps: Gently fold the crab into the filling. Place a portion on each wrapper with crab pieces in the center, fold into a square parcel and moisten the edge to seal.
Heat the oil over medium heat. Fry the rolls in batches, turning until crisp and golden with the filling thoroughly hot; drain well.
Mix the fish sauce with water, sugar, lime, garlic and chili. Serve the hot rolls with vermicelli and herbs.

keywords: Hải Phòng square crab spring rolls

banh-nam-hue.name: Huế flat rice cakes
aliases: Huế bánh nậm wrapped in banana leaves
banh-nam-hue.serving_basis: About 16 thin banana-leaf-wrapped rice cakes, steamed and served with chili fish sauce.
banh-nam-hue.description: Huế bánh nậm has a soft rice-flour layer spread thinly on banana or dong leaves, topped with shrimp and pork sautéed with shallots. Bếp Việt has adapted a thin-wrapped version, gently steamed and served with mild chili fish sauce.
banh-nam-hue.finished_dish: The cake is soft and smooth with a gentle banana-leaf aroma; a thin line of shrimp and pork filling brings mild savory-sweet flavor and a touch of pepper.
banh-nam-hue.serving: Unwrap while warm, scoop up each soft bite and dip it in fish sauce diluted with sugar, lime and chili.
banh-nam-hue.image_alt: Thin Huế rice cakes wrapped in banana leaves, two opened to reveal rice batter and shrimp-pork filling, served with chili fish sauce.
banh-nam-hue.time_note: Steaming time depends on cake thickness and quantity in the basket; Arrange the cakes apart to allow steam to circulate.
tips: Stir the batter over low heat until just thick enough to coat a spoon; it should remain smooth and spreadable.
Cook the filling until its moisture evaporates before spreading it on the batter; this helps the cakes hold their flat shape while steaming.
Brush the leaves lightly with oil and use a thin layer of batter to keep the cakes soft and flat.
search_terms: rice flour cake filled with shrimp and meat
keywords: Huế bánh nậm wrapped in banana leaves
rice flour cake filled with shrimp and meat

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Stir into the batter; add a little more if needed.

ingredients.name: Banana leaves
ingredients.notes: Wipe clean and warm until pliable for wrapping.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the filling and brushing the leaves.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use some to season the filling and the rest for dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Season the filling and dipping sauce.

preparation_steps: Wipe the banana leaves clean, warm them briefly until pliable, then cut them for wrapping. Mince the shrimp and prepare the ground pork, shallots and scallions.
Sauté the shallots and break up the pork. Add the shrimp, a little fish sauce, salt, sugar and pepper. Cook until the filling is dry, then mix in the scallions.
Whisk the rice flour with water and a little salt. Rest for about 10 minutes, then stir until smooth.
cooking_steps: Pour the batter into a heavy-bottomed pot. Stir constantly over low heat until slightly thickened and able to coat a spoon; remove it before it becomes stiff.
Brush the leaves with oil and spread a thin rectangle of batter on each. Add a little shrimp-pork filling down the center, then fold into a flat parcel.
Arrange the cakes in a steamer and steam for about 15–18 minutes, until the batter turns translucent and is cooked through. Rest for a few minutes and serve with the dipping sauce.

keywords: Huế bánh nậm wrapped in banana leaves
rice flour cake filled with shrimp and meat

banh-trang-xuc-hen-xao-hoi-an.name: Hội An stir-fried clams with rice crackers
aliases: Hoi An stir-fried clams with rice crackers
Hoi An clams with rice crackers
banh-trang-xuc-hen-xao-hoi-an.serving_basis: One sharing plate of stir-fried clams for four, served with toasted rice crackers for scooping.
banh-trang-xuc-hen-xao-hoi-an.description: Hến xào xúc bánh tráng is a familiar Hội An dish: small clams quickly stir-fried with shallots, garlic, Vietnamese coriander and seasonings, then scooped with crisp rice crackers. Bếp Việt adds roasted peanuts and a moderate amount of chili for a nutty, aromatic home-cooking version.
banh-trang-xuc-hen-xao-hoi-an.finished_dish: Small clams are tender and sweet, fragrant with shallots, garlic and Vietnamese coriander, with a nutty finish from peanuts. Crisp rice crackers add contrast.
banh-trang-xuc-hen-xao-hoi-an.serving: Serve the hot clams in a shallow dish, topped with peanuts and Vietnamese coriander. Break the rice crackers into scoop-sized pieces; sweet-and-sour fish sauce is optional.
banh-trang-xuc-hen-xao-hoi-an.image_alt: A plate of Hội An stir-fried clams with Vietnamese coriander, fried shallots and peanuts, served with crisp rice crackers for scooping.
banh-trang-xuc-hen-xao-hoi-an.time_note: Do not include cooking time for mussels if purchased in shell; Mussels must be cleaned of sand and cooked before use.
tips: If using live clams in their shells, rinse thoroughly, boil just until they open, remove the meat and drain well before stir-frying.
Stir-fry the clams briefly over high heat to preserve their sweetness and prevent excess liquid.
Add the Vietnamese coriander at the end and sprinkle on the peanuts just before serving.
keywords: Hội An stir-fried clams with rice crackers
Hoi An stir-fried clams with rice crackers
Hoi An clams with rice crackers

ingredients.name: Cleaned baby clam meat
ingredients.notes: Use more clams if buying them in their shells, then remove the meat after cooking.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander
ingredients.notes: Rinse clean and cut into suitable pieces.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: Can be used in the dipping sauce.

preparation_steps: Rinse the clam meat repeatedly to remove sand and drain well. If using clams in their shells, boil just until they open and remove the meat.
Slice the onion, shallots, garlic, chili and Vietnamese coriander. Roast and crush the peanuts, then prepare the toasted rice crackers.
Optionally make a dipping sauce with fish sauce, sugar, water, lime, garlic and chili.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add the onion and stir briefly until just translucent.
Add the clams, fish sauce, sugar and pepper. Stir-fry over high heat for 2–3 minutes until hot and just firm.
Turn off the heat and toss in the Vietnamese coriander and chili. Plate, sprinkle with peanuts and serve immediately with crisp rice crackers.

keywords: Hội An stir-fried clams with rice crackers

banh-san-dap-hoi-an.name: Hội An pounded cassava cakes
banh-san-dap-hoi-an.serving_basis: About eight chewy steamed cassava pieces topped with grated coconut and roasted peanuts, best served warm.
banh-san-dap-hoi-an.description: Hội An bánh sắn đập is made by pounding chewy cassava flat rather than mashing it, steaming it with grated coconut and finishing with roasted peanuts. Bếp Việt has adapted a home version with careful soaking and thorough cooking, preserving its earthy, lightly rich character.
banh-san-dap-hoi-an.finished_dish: Chewy, earthy cassava meets lightly rich coconut, crunchy roasted peanuts and a touch of salt that brings out its gentle sweetness.
banh-san-dap-hoi-an.serving: Arrange the warm cakes on a plate, top with grated coconut and crushed roasted peanuts, and add a pinch of salted sugar if desired.
banh-san-dap-hoi-an.image_alt: Soft, chewy Hội An cassava cakes topped with grated coconut and roasted peanuts on a ceramic plate.
banh-san-dap-hoi-an.time_note: Total time includes 30 minutes of soaking; Steaming time varies according to the thickness of the cassava pieces. Cassava must be prepared and fully cooked.
tips: Choose fresh, white-fleshed cassava with few fibers; remove the thick skin, pink inner layer and central woody core.
Soak the cassava in clean water for at least 30 minutes and discard the water. Steam until fully tender; never eat it undercooked.
Pound the cassava just enough to flatten it while keeping the fibers intact; do not mash it into a paste.
search_terms: steamed cassava with coconut and peanuts
keywords: steamed cassava with coconut and peanuts

ingredients.name: Peeled fresh cassava
ingredients.notes: Remove the fibrous core; weigh after peeling.

ingredients.name: Freshly grated coconut
ingredients.notes: Use mature but still moist coconut.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For soaking the cassava; discard the soaking water and do not reuse it.

preparation_steps: Remove the thick cassava skin and pink inner layer, cut away the fibrous core, rinse and cut into chunks. Soak in clean water for about 30 minutes, then discard the water.
Gently pound each cassava piece flat while keeping the fibers intact; do not mash. Roast and crush the peanuts, then mix with a little salt and sugar.
Clean the steamer and prepare the grated coconut. Discard cassava with an unusual odor, discoloration or unexpected bitterness.
cooking_steps: Arrange the flattened cassava in a steamer, layering some coconut between the pieces. Steam for 20–30 minutes until completely tender.
Remove the cassava while hot and arrange on a plate. Top with the remaining coconut and crushed roasted peanuts.
Taste and add a little sugar or salt if needed. Serve warm.

keywords: steamed cassava with coconut and peanuts
